title: Soccer Fever! The World Cup Kicks Off Tomorrow—Here's Your Cheat Sheet
summary: Imagine 48 countries all fighting for one golden trophy. That's what's happening starting tomorrow, June 11, when the 2026 FIFA World Cup kicks off! The first games are Mexico vs. South Africa and South Korea vs. Czech Republic. The U.S. team plays Paraguay on Friday at 9 p.m. ET. This is the biggest World Cup ever, with 48 men's national teams—16 more than last time. The first round, called the group stage, runs through June 27. There are 12 groups of four teams. Each team plays the other three in its group. A win gives you 3 points, a tie gives 1 point, and a loss gives 0. The top two teams from each group move on, plus the eight best third-place teams. After that, it's the knockout phase—lose once and you're out! The final is on July 19. If you want to watch, Fox and FS1 will show the games on TV. You can also stream them on the Fox One app with a paid subscription. Or, you can watch the opening ceremony and two early matches for free on Tubi. Tickets to see games in person are still available, but they're really expensive. Get ready for six weeks of amazing goals, huge saves, and nail-biting finishes!
why_it_matters: The World Cup shows how sports can connect people around the world, and you might even be inspired to play soccer with your friends or learn about different countries.

background_read: The World Cup is a soccer tournament held every four years, with teams from many countries competing for the championship.
The 2026 World Cup is the first to have 48 teams, and it is hosted by three countries together: the United States, Canada, and Mexico.
FIFA (the international organization that runs soccer events worldwide) organizes the World Cup, which started in 1930.

WHAT: The 2026 FIFA World Cup begins with a group stage, then a knockout phase, and ends with the final on July 19.
WHERE: Games can be watched on TV (Fox and FS1) or streamed through the Fox One app (paid) or Tubi (free for some matches).
WHY: The article explains how the tournament works, how to follow it, and that tickets are expensive, so fans can enjoy six weeks of exciting soccer.
